title: Ignite 2026: Codename MDASH code security in preview
summary: Microsoft says Codename MDASH, its agentic code security system, is in preview for eligible organizations. According to the Book of News it runs more than 100 specialised AI agents in a four-stage pipeline: map the attack surface, scan code, validate findings through agent debate and remove duplicates, and where possible reproduce a finding with a triggering input. New in this release: fewer low-quality results and false positives, repository sharding for large codebases, scan progress visibility, and support for more of the MAI Cyber model family, with MAI-Cyber-2 planned after evaluation.
why: This week's NGINX, PHP and Java fixes were largely found with AI-assisted research. Tools like MDASH point the same approach at your own code, which mostly affects teams that build internal apps, scripts and connectors.
todo: Do now: nothing to configure; note who owns application security for in-house code and scripts in your tenant.
If you evaluate it, start with a non-sensitive repository and agree who triages validated findings.
Wait: preview for eligible organizations only; eligibility, pricing and data handling are not described in the Book of News. Announced, not verified.
effective_note: Preview for eligible organizations — per Microsoft (announced, not verified).
